races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: Alpine Culture
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for James Owen who has no wins or placed finishes on Standard AW going in five attempts; Oisin Orr takes over but the surface record is a significant concern at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Lillie Margot
runners_data.note: Won last time at Goodwood over a mile and carries a tongue tie; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race in theory but all her form is on Good or Soft and she has no AW experience to call on here.|

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Charles Hills hold-up filly with two wins over ten furlongs; dropping in trip to a mile and switching to AW for the first time is the key question, though her placed Southwell form (twice at 8f on Standard) makes her the most credible closer in the field.|

runners_data.name: Picture Palace
runners_data.note: Style unclassified but has twice placed at Southwell over a mile on Standard ground with a tongue tie fitted; Josephine Gordon is a strong course jockey and the 51 days off is worth noting, though her Southwell form makes her a genuine player.|

runners_data.name: Decem Starr
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a tongue tie whose best form has come on Good or Soft; ten lengths off on her most recent Goodwood outing over 8f is not encouraging and she has no Southwell experience.|

runners_data.name: Areti
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Oliver Cole who has twice placed at Southwell over seven furlongs on Standard and now steps up to a mile; the headgear change to hood and tongue tie combination is eye-catching, and Lewis Edmunds takes over — she sets the pace and shapes this race.|

runners_data.name: Constant Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won at Southwell over 7f on Standard and placed there over 8f; the T14 strike rate of 2/18 is modest but Tom Clover has had this horse fit enough to place before on this track, and Jack Callan's 3lb claim could be pivotal.|

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.note: Unclassified in style with four consecutive placed or fourth finishes and no win; Grant Tuer's second string in the race alongside Lightening Lad, and the lack of victory combined with a modest T14 rate leaves questions unanswered.|

runners_data.name: Cliff Danger
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Pam Sly who has raced just three times and shown limited Southwell form with a best of seventh here over 8f on Standard; the ability to confirm hold on a pace role is uncertain given this record.|

runners_data.name: Lightning Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Simon & Ed Crisford who has three runs at Southwell over 8-10f all resulting in places but no win; three AW Standard runs without a win suggests she can set or press the pace without being a winning force.|

runners_data.name: Paranjape
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a Southwell win over 6f on Standard and three further placed finishes on this surface; David Egan's booking is significant and from a prominent position in a truly-run race he has the course form to be very dangerous.|

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with tongue tie and hood who has three Southwell runs placing twice at 8f on Standard; Richard Newland and Jamie Insole have a T14 rate of 3/29 but the consistent placed form at this track makes him one to respect.|

runners_data.name: Lightening Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Grant Tuer who placed at Southwell over 8f on Standard and over 7f; the T14 rate of 0/11 is alarming and a drop to OR 66 reflects a horse who has struggled since leaving the form book — hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Just A Gambler
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's prolific operator who is a genuine hold-up horse in nature but has been mapped to midfield due to the density of closers in this race; with seven days since his last run, Johnston's T14 rate of 10/72 is low for his yard, and a horse forced forward of his natural position in a truly-run race is unlikely to be at his best here.|

races.paceDynamic: Areti, Cliff Danger, and Lightning Glory are all confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field, meaning a contested, honest gallop is virtually guaranteed from the outset over this flat Southwell mile on Standard ground. These three will battle for supremacy in the early stages, ensuring the pace is genuine and unrelenting, which will stretch the field and expose any horse lacking stamina or tactical flexibility. With the fractions likely to be strong and the lead already contested before the first bend, prominent racers sitting just off the pace — Constant Star, Paranjape, Sovereign Bay — will be ideally positioned to pounce without expending energy fighting for the lead, giving them a meaningful positional advantage. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, with Just A Gambler a true closer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map; in a race run this fast, genuine hold-up horses will face a stern test of whether the pace truly collapses for them late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and a prominent racer sits just off the pace to pounce turning in.
scenarios.body: The contested lead will drain Areti, Cliff Danger, and Lightning Glory through the final two furlongs, leaving the horse who tracks them in second or third gear ideally placed; Constant Star and Sovereign Bay have the Southwell form and style to capitalise from this position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three lead horses breaks clear early and dictates at a more sustainable solo pace once rivals tire.
scenarios.body: Areti has shown consistent placed form on this surface and at this trip, and if the other two front-runners fade or are pulled back by riders who sense the pace is suicidal, Areti could convert stamina into victory; Constant Star or Paranjape pressing from behind would be the main danger.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the strong gallop is truly relentless and midfield horses who settle beautifully pick through tired rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kalokalo and Lillie Margot both have the ability to travel smoothly through a strongly-run race and have shown placings at a mile; the collapsing front end in the straight would open up gaps for a horse with a strong finish if ridden with patience.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so brutal that it entirely collapses and pure hold-up horses sweep past a spent field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Just A Gambler is a genuine hold-up type but is unlikely to secure its natural rear position in this shape, and Alpine Culture and Decem Starr have both struggled on this surface in similar conditions; this scenario is discounted because the true closers are compromised by the redistribution dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Areti, Cliff Danger, and Lightning Glory — monitor which of the three actually assumes the front rank at the start, as the horse that concedes the lead earliest will likely burn out first and cause significant positional chaos behind.|
Constant Star — Jack Callan's 3lb claim and Southwell course-and-distance form make this horse a key race shape beneficiary; if she settles just off the contested lead she could be the one to beat.|
Paranjape — David Egan's booking for a horse with a Southwell winning record and a strong T14 rate by comparison is a red flag to opposing runners; watch where he positions from the gate.|
Kalokalo — stepping onto AW for the first time and shortening in trip; how Jason Watson settles her in behind a fast pace will define whether her staying form translates to this very different test.|

Just A Gambler — watch whether Rob Hornby attempts to ride him closer than his natural style dictates; if the horse is forced wide or forward in the early scramble, his chance is compromised before the race truly begins.|

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Suhub
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter on Standard AW, finishing 2nd at Southwell over 10f and 7f, but races off the pace naturally and has been pushed into a midfield map position here — a shorter-than-ideal 7f in a false-pace race may not allow enough time to unleash its finishing effort; 21 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Symphony Of Joy
runners_data.note: Sole win came on turf (AW record is sparse) and recent form is modest (seventh and unplaced), with only one placed effort from five Standard-going runs — lacks the AW sharpness this race will likely demand; Oliver Stammers takes the ride for a yard with modest recent numbers.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Maestro
runners_data.note: 88-day absence is the obvious concern, and all five sim-going runs have produced zero wins and zero places on Standard AW; naturally a hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map, but its course record and layoff make this a significant ask under Charlie Johnston's yard at 3/29 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: Best profile in the field for this race shape — one win and four places from 11 Southwell/Standard runs, with both a win and a second at 7f on Standard; Dylan Hogan takes the ride and the horse clearly handles this track; though a hold-up type by style, its record suggests it travels well enough to fire in a bunch finish.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Gold
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with decent AW mileage but a mixed record — one win from 11 Standard-going starts and the recent form string (7-8-6-9-7) is uninspiring; headgear flag (visor) noted and Daniel Muscutt is a positive booking, but current trajectory is a concern in a competitive division.

runners_data.name: Surprised
runners_data.note: Switches to AW from turf/soft form, with all recent runs on Good or Soft — no Standard AW history visible in the sim-going data, so this is an unknown surface test; David Nolan is an asset and the yard has struggled recently (0/11 T14), making the handicap debut on Fibresand a speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Gunfighter
runners_data.note: David Egan in the saddle is an upgrade, but the horse has only one win and three places from 15 Standard-going starts and was pulled up or unplaced in its last two; mapped to midfield despite being a natural hold-up runner, and the style compromise may compound a patchy record at this level.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Knocker
runners_data.note: Wins have come at 6f on Soft and Good — stepping up to 7f on Standard Fibresand for a yard with no recent runners (T14: 0/0) is a significant unknown; a true rear-of-field horse by instinct placed into midfield on the map, and the trip/surface combination needs proving at Southwell specifically.

runners_data.name: Onemorenomore
runners_data.note: Placed twice from 15 Standard-going runs including a fifth at 7f Southwell, giving it some course context; Jason Hart is a capable AW jockey and 21 days' freshness is fine for a six-year-old; though naturally a hold-up type, its AW placed form gives it viable claims if the pace compresses into a sprint.

runners_data.name: Vitalline
runners_data.note: The only runner with an impressive AW strike rate — three wins and five places from 15 Standard-going starts, including a recent win at 6f on Standard; Josephine Gordon has course experience and the horse clearly thrives on Fibresand; most recent run just nine days ago is manageable; steps up slightly in trip from its winning distance but the form profile stands out.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 7f Southwell handicap, the race is likely to begin at a moderate tempo before coalescing into a prolonged sprint finish from the home turn. Every single runner carries a hold-up style designation, meaning the field will effectively self-regulate into a bunch race with no horse naturally driven to dictate — the pace will be manufactured by default rather than design. Anthropologist, Tennessee Gold and Surprised are the truest hold-up operators in the field and will look to track whatever modest gallop develops, while Suhub, Wadacre Maestro, Gunfighter, Jimmy Knocker, Onemorenomore and Vitalline are all redistributed from their natural rear-of-field role simply because the map has no space for them — in reality, some of those will be pushed wider and closer to the pace than usual. The tactical verdict is clear: with a genuinely contested, bunched tempo likely to produce a late sprint, horses with a clean turn of foot in the final two furlongs and a record of firing on Fibresand-standard AW surfaces hold the structural advantage — particularly those with proven Southwell or Standard-going form who can quicken from a pack rather than needing a true-run stamina test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunch Sprint, Late Kick
scenarios.trigger: If the field races as a compact group throughout and the race is decided by a single sharp burst in the final furlong
scenarios.body: With no pace injection from any single runner, the field will compress into a line approaching the home straight and the outcome will hinge purely on who quickens sharpest in the last 150 yards; horses with proven AW sharpness and current form hold the edge here

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Prominent Grabs It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed runners gets a comfortable lead by default and controls the race from the front at a sustainable clip
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop hands the initiative to whoever settles closest to the pace, and with Fibresand at Standard rewarding those who travel economically, a front-running opportunist who was never intended to lead could nick it with a clear passage

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Flat Track Sprint, Class Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely even and the race turns into a pure ability-based finish on Standard Fibresand
scenarios.body: Anthropologist's winning record at 7f on Standard surfaces and two placed efforts at Southwell make it the class pick in a sprint, while Tennessee Gold's AW experience gives it a platform

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Closers Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If the bunch races tightly and those further back are caught with no room to manoeuvre in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: With nearly every runner being a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield, those at the back of a compressed field face traffic risks that can derail their finish entirely, reducing the chances of the truest closers

watchPoints.text: Vitalline is the standout AW performer with three wins on Standard going and a win last time out — watch how Josephine Gordon positions it from the gate, as a forward move could turn this into a wire-to-wire effort at a big price.

Anthropologist holds the most compelling Southwell record in the field (1W4P from 11 sim-going runs) — if the race develops into the expected bunch sprint, it is structurally best placed to deliver in the final furlong.

Jimmy Knocker steps up sharply in trip to 7f on AW for the first time in this form cycle and represents a significant unknown — watch market moves given the yard has had zero runners in the past fortnight.

With every runner designated a hold-up style, watch the first two furlongs closely — whichever horse drifts to the front by default will have a significant positional advantage in what is forecast to be a slow-tempo, one-run race.

Wadacre Maestro returns from 88 days off with zero AW Standard-going place record from 10 attempts — if it drifts in the market pre-race, that likely confirms connections are cautious about its readiness.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Blazing Son
runners_data.note: Consistent Southwell form (2W5P on Standard over 7f) is the strongest angle here; naturally a deep hold-up type but will find himself racing in midfield given how many closers are in the field, meaning he may lack the finishing kick he needs to be at his most effective.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Recorded a course win at Southwell on Standard over 7f just two runs ago and returned a place last time; Lewis Edmunds takes over the reins and Iain Jardine has a solid 14-day strike-rate of 2/33 — his true style is from the rear but in this race he will likely be pushed into a more prominent pitch which could actually suit.

runners_data.name: Portman Blue
runners_data.note: All five runs on Standard going have produced a placed effort, indicating genuine surface affinity at 7f; a 66-day break is a notable query for fitness, and while his instinct is to come from behind, Jason Watson may find him racing mid-division rather than from the back in this pace scenario — tongue-tie worn.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Has a place at 6f on Standard but steps up to 7f where his record is thin; Antony Brittain yard is 0/12 over 14 days and he carries top weight of 135lbs — his hold-up style puts him at a disadvantage if the pace is as controlled as it looks.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Drops sharply back from 8-10f trips to 7f today, which is a trip he has not shown his best form over recently; Jason Hart is a positive booking for Michael Dods and there is some deeper Standard form (2W on sim-going at 9/15 tries) but the step down in trip feels like the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: Has run only on turf with Good or Soft going in his last five recorded runs, making this Standard Fibresand surface a significant and untested variable — the 0W0P on sim-going underlines that concern; David Egan is a quality booking but the horse's profile looks wrong for the track.

runners_data.name: Shamacid
runners_data.note: Boasts 12 runs on Standard going with eight places, suggesting he handles the surface well and runs consistently competitive races; he is a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield by the race shape, but his habit of finding something late is backed by that strong Southwell placing record — tongue-tie worn.

runners_data.name: Crystal Dagger
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's runner has been off 75 days and that layoff is the primary concern on what is already a modest OR of 60; instinctively a horse who wants to come from the back, but a 5-year-old apprentice in Taryn Langley and the redistribution into midfield both complicate his chances of producing his best.

runners_data.name: Reputation
runners_data.note: The 13-year-old veteran knows his job at Southwell — 2W5P from 13 Standard runs is an extraordinary course record and Ruth Carr has placed him with care; the sole front-runner here, Kaiya Fraser should be able to bowl along with a clean lead from stall one and control every aspect of the race from start to finish.

races.paceDynamic: Reputation is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7f handicap at Southwell and, with no rival willing or able to press from the front, she is set to dictate a solo, uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop that suits her perfectly — her record of 13 runs on Standard Fibresand with two wins and five places underlines her comfort in this environment. The hold-up horses behind her — Blazing Son, Pickersgill, Portman Blue, Shamacid and Crystal Dagger — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with closers and true back-of-the-field types, meaning most will race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates; Reputation is the horse most certain to actually secure her position. With a genuine lone leader controlling tempo and a Standard surface that rewards those tracking in behind without burning petrol, the tactical verdict is clear: horses who can sit second or third and make one smooth move from the top of the straight — genuine prominent-to-midfield profiles — are best placed, while confirmed hold-up finishers who need a true gallop to close into are compromised by the lack of genuine early pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Reputation Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Reputation leads uncontested from flag to finish at a fair but not suicidal clip, setting an entirely her own pace.
scenarios.body: Reputation controls every yard of the 7f trip, dictates the fractions and kicks clear entering the straight before her pursuers can organise a response; horses who tracked her in second and third are best placed to pick her off or follow her home, but she is hard to peg back given her course-and-distance form (2W5P at 13 tries on this surface).

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Reputation from second or third position throughout and delivers a sustained run from two furlongs out to overhaul her near the line.
scenarios.body: The even, unhurried gallop set by Reputation allows a well-positioned tracker to conserve energy and produce a clean finishing effort; Pickersgill (1W2P at Southwell on Standard) and Portman Blue (5/5 sim-going placings) are best suited having natural tactical speed to sit close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely slow enough that midfield horses find racing room and produce sustained late runs in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo briefly compresses the field in the straight but the redistribution of multiple true hold-up horses into midfield means traffic and interference reduce the effectiveness of late closers; Shamacid, with 12 Southwell Standard runs and eight places, shows the tenacity to grind through gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Field
scenarios.trigger: If Reputation is inconvenienced early or fails to stride freely, causing the whole pace structure to dissolve and turn the race into a messy, strongly-run sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Without a clear lead horse, multiple runners compete for position simultaneously, creating an unexpectedly strong gallop that suits a genuine hold-up finisher who can come from well off the pace; however, most confirmed closers here are racing out of role, limiting this scenario's potency.

watchPoints.text: Reputation's stall draw and lone front-running role is decisive — watch whether she gets away cleanly and immediately assumes the lead, as any stumble or slow start could fundamentally change the entire race shape.

Pickersgill and Portman Blue will both attempt to race prominently despite being natural hold-up horses — watch for a bunched, scrimmaging early phase as multiple horses try to sit second and third, which could cause interference and unsettle Reputation's rhythm.

Noble Guest has zero form on Standard going (0W0P on sim-going across two runs) — watch for whether he handles the surface at all, as a horse who consistently races on turf can find Fibresand unpredictable under foot.

King Of Fury represents a significant step down in trip from 8-10f to 7f — watch his early running to see whether Jason Hart rides him up with the pace or allows him to settle, as his recent form has been over much longer distances.

Crystal Dagger is returning from a 75-day absence for a small yard with 0/6 over 14 days — watch the market for any support, as cold money for a well-rested horse from a less active yard can be significant at this level.

runners_data.name: Naana's Sparkle
runners_data.note: Prominent-style filly with strong Southwell-related form in terms of similar going, has won at 5f on soft/heavy and placed on good; wears hood, last ran 29 days ago which is a comfortable return window, and is well suited by a race that plays to early positional pace.

runners_data.name: Rapper's Delight
runners_data.note: Won over 5f at Southwell on Standard previously and returns having run just eight days ago, so fitness is obvious; prominent runner who goes well on this surface but recent AW form shows a nine-length beating on same course, suggesting current form needs treating with caution.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: In-form stable (Easterby, 5 wins from 41 in 14 days) sends this five-year-old back to Southwell where it has course experience; naturally a prominent racer, it will likely find itself shuffled wider than ideal in a field stacked with similar types — its 0.94 style-fit flag reflects the difficulty of getting its customary pitch.

runners_data.name: Buzz Box
runners_data.note: Three wins at Southwell AW in its last five starts over this trip makes the course-and-distance profile compelling; returned after 164 days off and ran fourth last time so fitness is improving, though as a genuine prominent type now operating in a deeper map position, its ability to replicate those wins depends on a different pace shape emerging.

runners_data.name: Cloud King
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's hold-up runner has won and placed multiple times at Southwell over 5f, giving it the strongest course profile among the closers; back after 197 days off is the key concern — it has not been seen since last autumn and trainer has had no winners from eight runners in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Blinky
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, and the Southwell AW form figures include a placed effort, but recent strings (8004) show modest current form; wears a hood-style headgear designation and was beaten at least eight lengths in its last two visits here, making it hard to fancy in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to bring it into contention.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 94 and the confirmed lone pace-setter over five furlongs; Jamie Spencer is an astute front-riding judge when the occasion demands it, and Kylian's Southwell AW experience is relevant, though its style-fit tag (0.93) is a pace-type flag rather than a redistribution — this horse is simply rated slightly below its best when truly pressed.

runners_data.name: Tropical Storm
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up horse has not run since 53 days ago and has no Southwell AW going data in its recent history; all five recent runs have come on good or softer turf, making Standard AW a surface question mark, and its form figures (09-830) suggest it is returning from a quiet spell rather than peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Alligator Alley
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with four wins and six places from 15 starts on similar going — that strike rate is one of the best in the field; has won twice at 5f on Standard AW and is prominent in style, placing it right in the mix for the early positions in a field where the front-rank battle is the defining tactical story.

races.paceDynamic: Kylian is the confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — Naana's Sparkle, Rapper's Delight, and Alligator Alley are all prominent-style horses but none are natural blazing lead-seekers who will force Kylian off his rhythm over five furlongs at Southwell. That creates a scenario where Kylian can bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop under Jamie Spencer, dictating terms from the outside of the front-rank group. This field contains more prominent-biased horses than can all secure their preferred position: Canon's House and Buzz Box are genuine prominent types but have been redistributed to midfield in this map because Kylian, Naana's Sparkle, Rapper's Delight, and Alligator Alley are more likely to hold the early real estate, and those two will be forced to settle deeper than ideal. A race run at a measured, controlled tempo over the minimum trip on Standard ground strongly favours horses who can race close to the pace without expending excessive early energy — prominent and pressing types with tactical versatility hold the structural edge, while true hold-up runners like Cloud King, Blinky, and Tropical Storm face an uphill task if the pace is never brisk enough to bring them into the race late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kylian Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kylian is allowed to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop and the field fails to generate genuine pressure through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Kylian bowls along under Spencer making all, setting a pace comfortable enough to preserve reserves for the final furlong, and the hold-up horses never get the strong pace they need to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Pegs Back
scenarios.trigger: If Naana's Sparkle, Rapper's Delight, or Alligator Alley travel powerfully enough to challenge Kylian from two furlongs out and turn it into a sprint.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes competitive rather than truly contested, with the prominent group running to their ratings and one of the tracking horses picking up sharply when Kylian's effort flattens late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough — more by accident than design — that the field strings out and the hold-up runners get a true run-in.
scenarios.body: Cloud King or Buzz Box, who have both won over this course and distance, find the track opening late and motor home past a tiring vanguard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Place Shock
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant early jostling for position that disrupts Kylian's rhythm and the race fragments into a messy, ragged contest with no clean pace shape.
scenarios.body: A beneficiary emerging from midfield or a front-runner pegging on gamely in a muddled finish; Canon's House, forced wide of its natural role, could profit from positional confusion if the field shuffles.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Canon's House or Buzz Box can find any daylight from their mapped midfield positions — if either gets caught in traffic through the first two furlongs, their natural prominent instinct could cause them to overcorrect and use too much energy.

Cloud King returns after 197 days off for a trainer with zero wins from eight runners in the past 14 days — monitor the market carefully; any significant drift at the off would confirm it is likely underdone.

Tropical Storm has no recent form on AW Standard going and all five latest runs are on turf; if it fails to handle the surface switch, it could impede or interfere with hold-up runners attempting to close late.

Buzz Box's 164-day absence followed by a running-on fourth last time suggests it is sharpening up — if it gets a clean passage from its mapped position and the pace quickens late, its three previous Southwell wins signal it cannot be wholly dismissed in Scenario C.

runners_data.name: John Galt
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's four-year-old wears a tp hood and is the most likely horse to take up a forward berth by default; two places from two Standard runs and a recent second at Goodwood over 1m2f suggest he stays and handles the going, though his form peak is at shorter trips than today's 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Baltic
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes over on this Lucy Wadham six-year-old who has two wins and three places from 15 Standard-ground starts — the most relevant surface profile in the field; genuine hold-up style suits a compressed pace scenario, though his last three runs include two soft-ground outings where he has disappointed.

runners_data.name: Senor Cortez
runners_data.note: John Butler's five-year-old is ideally drawn for this trip with five of his last six runs over 1m6f and a strong placing record — 1W4P from 13 similar-going starts; prominent racer who should travel smoothly off what figures to be a modest gallop, giving Jack Callan (3lb claim) every chance to conserve energy.

runners_data.name: Premier
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's four-year-old has a genuinely prominent style but the field configuration means he is unlikely to slot into his natural front-rank position; his best form includes a win over 1m6f on Good and a placed effort on Heavy, but zero places from 15 Standard runs is a stark flag, and Greatrex's 14-day record of 0/11 adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Spooky Wooky
runners_data.note: Simon West's three-year-old is a true hold-up horse but the map has placed her in midfield given the congestion at the rear; 242 days off the track is the standout concern, and while she has placed over this trip on Soft and Good, she has never won on Standard and carries a lightweight of 131lbs for a yard running 0/1 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Shushi
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old is unproven on style (tagged U) and unproven at 1m6f — her furthest win was listed at 1m1f — but Balding's yard is in excellent form (10/58 over 14 days) and PJ McDonald is a quality booking; Southwell AW is a new environment for her and that uncertainty tempers any optimism despite the stable angle.

runners_data.name: Tripoli Flyer
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — the confirmed front-runner for this race has been withdrawn, fundamentally altering the pace map and removing the only horse who would have set a genuine early gallop; all race shapes must now be recalibrated around a field with no natural pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Dino Bellagio
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's seven-year-old has a proven hold-up profile and one win plus two places from 15 Standard-going starts; a 22-day turnaround is acceptable, and last time out he finished third over 1m6f on Soft, suggesting he handles stamina tests — David Nolan's booking is a positive at a track where tactical patience is rewarded.

races.paceDynamic: With Tripoli Flyer listed as a non-runner, this 1m6f Southwell contest loses its confirmed front-runner, leaving a field dominated by prominent and hold-up types with no natural pace-setter. John Galt and Senor Cortez are the likeliest candidates to press forward from the prominent bracket, though neither has a strong front-running profile, meaning the pace is likely to be steady to moderate early before the tempo lifts in the back straight. Baltic, Dino Bellagio, and Spooky Wooky all want to come from off the pace, but Premier and Spooky Wooky are redistributed prominent and hold-up types respectively — both unable to secure their natural positions — meaning the race shape is muddled at the rear. The tactical verdict is clear: with a moderate, uncontested gallop likely from John Galt or Senor Cortez, this race favours hold-up horses with a strong staying finish, as a false early pace will compress the field and reward those able to produce a sustained late run over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If John Galt or Senor Cortez sets a modest, uncontested gallop that compresses the field and sets up a stamina-test finish.
scenarios.body: With no genuine front-runner to force the tempo, the race drifts along at a sedate clip before quickening in the straight, handing the advantage to hold-up horses with proven staying ability over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Control
scenarios.trigger: If John Galt dictates from the front at a genuine clip and the prominent duo grind down the opposition with a sustained gallop.
scenarios.body: John Galt's recent Goodwood form over 1m4f-1m6f and Senor Cortez's consistent placing record at this trip suggest they can dominate if they control tempo honestly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Loomer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow early and a strong late finisher explodes from the rear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Baltic has two wins and three placings from 15 starts on Standard going and carries Spencer's tactical intelligence, while Dino Bellagio has a win and two places from 15 Standard starts and a recent Southwell placing run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners jostle for position in the absence of a confirmed leader, creating a stop-start gallop and a muddling race.
scenarios.body: Without Tripoli Flyer to dictate, the lack of a natural pacesetter could produce an erratic pace that unsettles all running styles and hands an unpredictable outcome to a horse produced with a single decisive move.

watchPoints.text: With Tripoli Flyer a non-runner, watch whether John Galt or Senor Cortez attempts to fill the pace-setting void — whoever takes the lead effectively controls the tempo and dictates which running style is advantaged.

Baltic's record shows two wins and three places on Standard going but consecutive poor efforts on Soft suggest Jamie Spencer may need to hunt a specific position early — if he gets caught in traffic in a compressed field, his late run may come too late over 1m6f.

Premier's complete absence of Standard-going form (0/15 places) combined with a style-fit discount from redistribution means that if he is prominent early and meets a genuine gallop, he may be vulnerable in the closing stages.

Dino Bellagio and Baltic represent the two most experienced Standard-going hold-up horses in the field — if they settle smoothly in the early stages and the tempo is modest, their finishing kicks become the dominant shape for the closing stretch.

Spooky Wooky's 242-day layoff is the longest absence in the field — watch her behaviour in the paddock and early race demeanour, as a ring-rusty display could compromise whatever tactical plan Simon West has set.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Club Class
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who has finished first or second in her last two Fibresand starts (TP headgear); the danger is her OR=81 mark may be vulnerable if she uses energy establishing the lead, but without a challenger she is ideally placed to control.|

runners_data.name: Jupiter Ammon
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who has been redistributed onto the pace map at midfield due to field congestion at the rear — PJ McDonald takes over here, and the horse's best form on Southwell AW (3rd, 1m1f) is encouraging, though the lack of a win on Standard is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Forever Penywern
runners_data.note: 290 days off is a significant flag, especially with 61 jockey days listed — Warren and Edward Greatrex combination usually have their horses fit when running, but all five recent runs were on Good or Soft ground over much longer trips, making this 1m3f Fibresand assignment a genuine stylistic leap.|

runners_data.name: Aulis
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's mount has the strongest Fibresand credentials in the field with a win on Standard going and four placed efforts across AW and turf; Tina Jackson's low T14 strike rate (0/3) is a minor negative but the horse's form figures of 2-1-2-2 on similar surfaces represent consistent quality.|

runners_data.name: Vaguer
runners_data.note: Returns after a 526-day absence with an unknown fitness level and only lightly-raced form to go on — the UNKNOWN going tag reflects genuine uncertainty; the 7lb claimer Arron D'Arcy is tasked with reintroducing a horse for James Fanshawe, whose 6/24 T14 record suggests moderate current yard momentum.|

runners_data.name: Victors Spirit

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage

runners_data.name: Crystal Mariner
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the mount on this 6-year-old who has won twice on Fibresand including a 1m1f success on Standard — the 6-day turnaround is tight but not disqualifying; an OR=82 mark is highest in the field alongside Northwest Passage, and his sim-going record of 2W3P represents the most compelling Fibresand CV among the hold-up horses.|

races.paceDynamic: Club Class is the sole confirmed front runner here and, racing on Fibresand at Southwell over 1m3f on a Standard surface, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any serious challenger for the lead. Forever Penywern, Aulis, and Jupiter Ammon all carry prominent or hold-up tags, but Jupiter Ammon and Victors Spirit are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map — the field carries more hold-up types than the pace shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, and Northwest Passage and Crystal Mariner are the most likely to genuinely settle deep as true closers. With a single pace-setter controlling the tempo without pressure, this race is set up as a procession from the front for much of the 1m3f trip, and the tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can track Club Class and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out are best placed, while true hold-up horses will need a strong pace injection that is simply unlikely to materialise here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Club Class Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Club Class leads from the outset and sets a steady, uncontested tempo that suits those tracking close.
scenarios.body: Club Class dictates from stall to straight, keeping fractions controlled on Standard Fibresand; horses pressing from second and third position — Aulis and Forever Penywern — are ideally placed to pounce inside the final two furlongs as the pace never genuinely quickens for the deep closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Aulis or Forever Penywern press Club Class firmly from early and the race develops into a sustained two-furlong duel up front.
scenarios.body: A moderate but not dawdling gallop set by Club Class invites those tucked just behind to kick early, with Aulis's proven Southwell form and Fibresand wins making her particularly dangerous in this shape; Forever Penywern's stamina profile over marathon trips on Good could translate to a bold show at this shorter trip on a flat, fast surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If Club Class sets a genuinely strong early gallop that strings the field out and leaves a meaningful gap for closers to close.
scenarios.body: Northwest Passage and Crystal Mariner, the most genuine hold-up runners in the race, would benefit if the tempo is high enough to stop those prominent horses sustaining their effort; Crystal Mariner's two Fibresand wins and Northwest Passage's recent second on this surface give them each an argument in this less-likely shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Vaguer Lands Plot
scenarios.trigger: If Vaguer, returning from 526 days off, bounces back with a sharp fresh-horse performance and travels powerfully in midfield throughout.
scenarios.body: With a lightly-raced profile and unknown current form, Vaguer is a complete wildcard — a fresh horse returning at peak fitness could outrun a field that takes each other on; the 7lb claimer Arron D'Arcy adds tactical uncertainty but also removes dead weight for a horse whose best form shows a win and a placed effort.

watchPoints.text: Club Class sets the race up entirely — watch whether she dictates a truly solo, pressure-free lead or is pressed into the first bend by Aulis and Forever Penywern, as this single variable determines whether the race suits front or prominent horses.

Forever Penywern has not run in 290 days and all five recent starts were on Good or Soft ground over marathon distances — watch market moves as late money would suggest yard confidence that current fitness justifies this significant surface and trip change.

Vaguer is a 526-day absentee on UNKNOWN going with a claim jockey — a big early price collapse into the market would be a strong signal that James Fanshawe has the horse primed, given the trainer's typically patient approach with lightly-raced horses.

Crystal Mariner and Northwest Passage are the genuine hold-up horses in this field — watch their position at the halfway point; if Club Class has built a decisive lead by that stage, both are likely to need a pace collapse that the race shape simply does not favour.

Victors Spirit and Jupiter Ammon are both natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield through redistribution — if either is seen pushing forward unusually early under their experienced jockeys (Hornby, McDonald), it signals a deliberate tactical switch that could reframe the pace picture entirely.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On X Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Charlie Johnston with solid course form at this sort of trip, showing three placed efforts from eleven starts at Standard going; Daniel Muscutt takes the ride after just eight days off, and the blinkers on likely sharpen the horse's focus, though a steady pace set by a lone front-runner may not create enough tempo to fully unleash a late run from the rear.

runners_data.name: Alrazeen
runners_data.note: Keiran Burke's five-year-old has been off 136 days — a notable return from a lengthy break — and posted a narrow win twice at this Standard Fibresand track, though its genuine hold-up style means it has been shown in midfield on the map because the field carries more rear-of-field types than the race shape can place at the back; on a quiet-tempo scenario, racing further forward than natural is an imperfect fit.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner for the Simon & Ed Crisford yard, and Callum Rodriguez can exploit a completely uncontested lead over this stamina trip; limited course form here (2/10 at Standard) tempers confidence slightly, but the tactical advantage of uncontested lead on Fibresand over 2m½f is significant and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that it may ultimately race further back than ideal depending on pace decisions.

runners_data.name: New York Minute
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's four-year-old carries the visor and is placed three times from fourteen starts on Standard going, with a most recent run suggesting a return to form after a 35-day break; a prominent runner who could sit just off Boatswain, Jamie Spencer may opt for a stalking role over this marathon trip rather than forcing the issue, which keeps the horse in a strong tactical position if the pace stays honest.

runners_data.name: Sixpack
runners_data.note: James Owen's six-year-old arrives in excellent recent form — three wins from five runs — but all those victories have come at shorter trips (12-14f) on Good or Soft ground, and the step up to 2m½f on Fibresand represents a notably different stamina test with zero course form recorded; Oisin Orr takes the ride and the hold-up style suits a strong pace, but the concern is whether this horse's finishing kick translates over an extra distance on an artificial surface.

races.paceDynamic: Boatswain is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field over 2m½f on Southwell's Fibresand, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Callum Rodriguez can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. New York Mile is a second prominent type who may sit just off Boatswain and apply some company, but is unlikely to force a breakneck tempo at this stamina-sapping trip. The three hold-up horses — Sax Appeal, Alrazeen, and Sixpack — will track from midfield to rear, relying on Boatswain setting enough pace to set up a meaningful finish; with only one genuine front-runner, the pace may be conservative and the race could develop into a tactical crawl before a late sprint, which typically favours those who have been prominent and can kick early rather than deep closers needing a true test. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, with Alrazeen redistributed to midfield on the map; in practice, Boatswain is best placed to control the lead with New York Minute the most likely to secure the second prominent berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boatswain Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Boatswain leads without serious pressure and controls the tempo throughout the 2m½f trip.
scenarios.body: Rodriguez dictates a measured gallop from the front, and with no rival forcing the issue, Boatswain can conserve energy before quickening entering the straight; prominent racers who have tracked the steady pace are ideally placed to pounce in the final furlong. Horses who have raced close to the pace without expending early energy will be best positioned to challenge, making the prominent profile the dominant winning shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Boatswain sets a genuinely strong gallop that strings the field out and creates a true stamina test in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end pace would drain Boatswain's reserves and allow the hold-up horses to reel him in over the final two furlongs; Sixpack, whose in-form record shows three wins from five recent starts, and Sax Appeal, with course-applicable hold-up form, would benefit most from this scenario. However, this shape depends on a pace scenario that is unlikely given only one front-runner in the field, limiting this outcome's probability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Boatswain sets a very slow early tempo that bunches the field and turns the race into a sprint over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A crawl-and-sprint over 2m½f on the flat would compress the field and reduce the race to a battle of raw finishing speed rather than stamina; New York Minute's two-runner sprint credentials and Sixpack's recent winning form under similar conditions give them a live chance in a contested late dash. This scenario is problematic for genuine hold-up horses who need momentum built earlier in the race, and the redistribution of Alrazeen to midfield means it is not positioned to exploit a sprint finish as effectively as its natural style might otherwise allow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If New York Minute challenges Boatswain vigorously from the front and both prominent horses quicken clear of the field in the straight.
scenarios.body: If New York Minute pushes up aggressively to contest the lead, the race becomes a two-horse match up front and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up in the short Southwell straight; this scenario isolates the closers and rewards front-running stamina. This is the least likely shape given New York Minute's hold-up profile at longer trips, but remains a fringe possibility if Jamie Spencer opts for an aggressive front-ranking ride.

watchPoints.text: Boatswain is the sole front-runner in a five-horse field — if Rodriguez senses zero pressure and slows the gallop dramatically in the early stages, the race could become a sprint in the final two furlongs that may not suit the confirmed hold-up horses at all.

Sixpack's recent form figures (-31311) look impressive but all winning runs came at 12-14f on turf; watch for signs of the horse not staying the full 2m½f Fibresand trip, which could see the finishing run flatten out before the line.

Alrazeen returns from 136 days off — the longest layoff in the field — and while Keiran Burke has form with fresh horses (3W5P similar-going), a horse resuming from nearly five months off in a race where it may not get its natural position at the rear is a meaningful fitness and tactical risk.

New York Minute wears a visor for the first time today; if Jamie Spencer uses it to sharpen the horse's early concentration and commits to a close-tracking role behind Boatswain rather than dropping out, this could shift the tactical shape of the race significantly from a two-runner battle to a closer contest entering the straight.

The Southwell straight is short and the track configuration means horses that have been prominent throughout are historically advantaged in small fields over marathon trips — watch whether the hold-up trio (Sax Appeal, Sixpack, Alrazeen) have enough runway from their rearward positions to close the gap if Boatswain conserves energy throughout.
